walkthroughs.body_html:
Voice of the Genome — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Voice of the Genome brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Voice of the Genome.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.
It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.

mcqs.q: Why is a reflex action faster than a conscious response?
options: Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
The brain decides reflexes faster than other actions because it skips thinking.
The signal does not need to be processed by the brain — it travels through a simpler reflex arc via the spinal cord.
Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
